raw_text:
Below is a 12-week, 3x/week strength plan (plus 1–2 optional low‑impact conditioning sessions) built around your client’s restrictions: no jumping, and no deep knee flexion under load. It emphasizes controlled ROM, closed-chain quad strength, hip/hamstring power, lateral stability, and trunk control to prepare for ski demands. All sessions include a warm-up. Progress ROM only if pain ≤2/10 during and after, no effusion/swelling the next day, and quality movement (no valgus collapse). If symptoms flare, reduce ROM or load and hold progression.

Global guardrails
- ROM limits: Weeks 1–4 target knee flexion ≤45–60° under load; Weeks 5–8 ≤60–70°; Weeks 9–12 up to 70–80° if symptom-free. Use box/bench/seat height to control depth. No forced end-range, no twisting/pivoting on the right knee.
- Tempo and isometrics: Use slower eccentrics and strategic isometrics early to load tissue safely.
- Progression: Increase load 2.5–5% per week when reps are completed with good form and no knee reaction. Every 4th week is a lighter/deload week.
- Weekly schedule example: Mon = Lower A (quad-dominant, closed chain), Wed = Upper + Core/Carry, Fri = Lower B (hinge/unilateral/lateral control). Optional Sat/Sun conditioning (Zone 2, sleds, slideboard later).

Standard warm-up (10–12 minutes each session)
- 5 min bike/elliptical, seat high to limit knee flexion.
- Tissue/activation: 1) Banded terminal knee extensions (TKE) 2x20/side; 2) Mini-band lateral walks 2x15 m; 3) Heel-elevated bodyweight box squats to high box 2x8 slow (3-0-3); 4) Ankle rocks and calf pulses 1–2 min.
- Prep core: Pallof iso holds 2x20s/side.

PHASE 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation, tolerance, controlled ROM
Goal: Build quad strength in safe angles, hip/hamstring base, lateral hip/adductor strength, balance and trunk control. Emphasize tempo and isometrics.

Week 1
Day 1 – Lower A (quad/closed chain)
- Box squat (high box; goblet or safety-bar) 3x6–8, 3-0-3 tempo, RPE 6, knee ≤45–50°
- Reverse sled drag (upright torso) 4x20–25 m, moderate effort
- Leg press (feet high/neutral, 0–60° ROM) 3x10, 2-1-2 tempo
- Spanish squat isometric (strap/band, ~40–45° knee) 3x30–40s
- Standing calf raise 3x12–15
- Pallof press 3x10/side

Day 2 – Upper + Core/Carry
- DB incline press 4x6–8 @ RPE 7
- Chest-supported row 4x8–10
- Half-kneeling landmine press 3x8/side
- Lat pulldown (neutral grip) 3x10–12
- Face pull 3x12–15
- Farmer carry 4x30–40 m
- Side plank 3x25–30s/side

Day 3 – Lower B (hinge/unilateral/lateral)
- Trap bar deadlift from 4–6" blocks 4x5, RPE 6–7
- RDL 3x8, 3-sec eccentric
- Low box step-up (6–8", upright shin) 3x6/side, slow eccentric
- Hip thrust (barbell or DB) 3x8–10
- Short-lever Copenhagen side plank 3x8–10/side (2-sec top hold)
- Single-leg balance with reach (Y-pattern, shallow) 3x5 reaches/leg

Optional conditioning (1–2x this week): 20–30 min Zone 2 bike/elliptical; finish with TKE 2x20.

Week 2
- Repeat Week 1 with: +1 set on first main lift each lower day (Box squat 4 sets; Trap bar 5 sets), increase sled drag load slightly; add Band TKE finisher 2x20 on Day 1.

Week 3
- Box squat: progress to slightly lower box if symptom-free (≤55–60°), 4x5–6 @ RPE 7.
- Reverse sled drag heavier 5x20 m.
- Leg press 4x8 (slightly more load).
- Add Seated knee extension (short-arc 30–0°) 2x15 light, slow.
- Add Lateral step-down (4–6" box, partial ROM) 3x6/side Day 3, control valgus.
- Balance: add light cable/band perturbations.

Week 4 (deload)
- Drop volume to ~70% (remove 1–2 sets per lift), keep intensity moderate; hold ROM; no new ROM increases this week.

PHASE 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength and capacity (ROM-controlled)
Goal: Heavier loading within safe angles; progress unilateral control; increase sled volume; introduce shallow split patterns and adductor capacity.

Week 5
Day 1 – Lower A
- Safety-bar box squat (box height as per Week 3) 5x3–5 @ RPE 7–8
- Heavy reverse sled drag 6x20 m
- Leg press (60–70° max if tolerated) 4x6–8
- Spanish squat ISO 3x40–50s
- Standing calf raise 4x10–12
- Pallof press with step-out 3x8/side

Day 2 – Upper + Core/Carry
- Bench press 5x3–5 @ RPE 7–8
- One-arm DB row 4x8/side
- Seated DB shoulder press 3x8–10
- Wide-grip pulldown 3x8–10
- Prone T/Y/W 2x12 each
- Suitcase carry 4x25–30 m/side
- Dead bug 3x8/side

Day 3 – Lower B
- Trap bar deadlift from 2–4" blocks 5x3–5 @ RPE 7–8
- RDL 3x6–8
- Front-foot elevated split squat (small elevation, shallow ROM) 3x6/side, upright torso, slow eccentric
- Hip thrust 4x6–8 (heavier)
- Hamstring curl (seated or prone) 3x8–10, 3-sec eccentric
- Copenhagen (medium lever) 3x6–8/side

Conditioning: 25–30 min Zone 2 + backward treadmill walk (1–2% incline) 2x3–4 min.

Week 6
- Add 2.5–5% load to main lifts if pain-free.
- Increase split squat to 4x6/side if tolerated.
- Add Band TKE 3x15 between leg press sets.
- Balance: Single-leg RDL reach (BW) 2x6/side as primer Day 3.

Week 7
- Box squat: maintain depth, 6x3 @ RPE 8 (speed focus, crisp).
- Trap bar from low blocks 6x2–3 @ RPE 8 (clean reps).
- Leg press 4x6 heavy; drop Spanish squat iso to 2x40s.
- Lateral step-down (6–8" box, still partial) 3x6–8/side.
- Add Lateral sled drag (belt or straps) 4x15–20 m/side, upright, shallow knee bend.

Week 8 (deload)
- Reduce sets by ~40–50%, keep a touch of intensity (RPE 6–7), keep ROM the same.
- Extra recovery emphasis this week: add easy mobility and Zone 2 only.

PHASE 3 (Weeks 9–12): Strength-to-power (no jumping), ski-specific lateral control and endurance
Goal: Maintain/intensify strength, add safe “power” via sleds, med-ball, hip-hinge speed; add slideboard intervals and isometric “ski” positions at shallow angles; gradually expand ROM to tolerance (not exceeding ~80°).

Week 9
Day 1 – Lower A (strength + isometric endurance)
- Safety-bar box squat 5x3–4 @ RPE 8 (if completely symptom-free, box 1–2 cm lower, still ≤70–75°)
- Reverse sled drag heavy 6x20–25 m
- Leg press 3x6 heavy + 1 back-off set 1x12 lighter
- Iso “ski hold” wall sit (35–45° knee) with weight shifts L↔R, 3x40–50s
- Standing calf raise 4x10–12
- Pallof press ISO 3x20–25s/side

Day 2 – Upper + Power Core
- Bench press 4x4–5 @ RPE 8
- Chest-supported row 4x6–8 heavy
- Half-kneeling landmine press 3x6–8/side (add band for accommodating resistance if available)
- Med-ball chest pass to wall (heavy, seated) 4x6
- Anti-rotation med-ball hold (standing, feet parallel) 3x20s/side
- Farmers or front-rack carry 4x30–40 m

Day 3 – Lower B (hinge power + lateral)
- Trap bar deadlift from floor if tolerated, or low blocks 5x3 @ RPE 8, fast concentric
- Kettlebell swing (hip hinge, shallow knees) 4x10, RPE 6–7 (only if pain-free; otherwise sub banded hip hinge 4x8)
- Single-leg RDL 3x6/side controlled
- Lateral sled drag 5x15–20 m/side
- Hamstring curl 3x8–10 (2-sec pause at curl)
- Copenhagen (medium/long lever as tolerated) 3x6–8/side

Conditioning: Introduce slideboard if available, shallow stance, no abrupt stops. 6–8 rounds: 20s on/40s off at easy-moderate intensity. If no slideboard, do lateral band shuffles 4x20 m + bike 15–20 min.

Week 10
- Increase box squat and trap bar by 2.5–5%.
- Leg press 4x6 heavy.
- Wall-sit ski hold progress to 3x50–60s with gentle poling motion (light dowels) to mimic stance changes.
- KB swing 5x10 if tolerated; otherwise maintain alternative.
- Add Heels-elevated goblet squat to high box 2x10 as a very controlled quad finisher.

Week 11
- Strength emphasis peak
  - Box squat 6x2–3 @ RPE 8–8.5 (fast but clean).
  - Trap bar 6x2 @ RPE 8–8.5.
  - Reverse sled drag 6x20–30 m heavy.
- Lateral step-down 3x8/side (controlled; consider slightly higher box if perfect control).
- Slideboard: 8–10 rounds 20s on/40s off (moderate), stay shallow.
- Add Anti-rotation march (cable) 3x12 steps/side.

Week 12 (taper/consolidate)
- Reduce volume ~40%. Keep intensity moderate-high on first main lift each day (RPE 7–8) to retain strength.
- Reconfirm ROM stays within comfort (≤75–80°). No new ROM this week.
- Finish sessions with ski-specific isometrics: 2x45–60s wall-sit shifts + 2x20s lateral isometric holds (partial lateral lunge hold, shallow angle) each side.
- Conditioning: 1–2 easy Zone 2 rides, 20–30 min; 1 short slideboard session 6x20s/40s at easy pace.

Exercise library and notes by goal
- Quad/closed-chain: Box squat variants, reverse sled drag, leg press partial ROM, Spanish squat iso, TKE. Control tibial rotation and valgus.
- Hinge/hamstrings/glutes: Trap bar deadlift from blocks/floor, RDL, hip thrust, hamstring curl.
- Lateral/adductors: Lateral step-downs (partial), lateral sled drags, Copenhagen progressions, slideboard intervals (shallow).
- Core/anti-rotation: Pallof press/iso, anti-rotation march, carries, side planks, dead bugs.
- “Power” without jumping: Heavy sled work, fast concentric on main lifts, med-ball throws (seated/half-kneel), hip-hinge velocity (KB swing) if tolerated.

Optional low-impact conditioning (1–2x/week throughout)
- Zone 2: Bike/elliptical 20–35 min, RPE 5–6/10.
- Sled circuits: Push or drag 5–8 rounds of 20–30 m with 60–90s rest.
- Later phase: Slideboard intervals as outlined.

Recovery and monitoring
- Swelling/pain rules: If pain >2/10 during or persists >24 h, or swelling increases, reduce ROM and/or load next session; hold progression until calm.
- Session RPE target: 6–8 on main lifts; assistance 6–7.
- Soft tissue/mobility: 5–8 min post-session on calves, quads, adductors, glutes. Gentle knee flexion/extension active ROM (pain-free).
- Sleep and steps: Aim 7–9 h sleep; daily easy walking as tolerated on flat ground.

Criteria to progress depth and complexity
- No effusion and ≤2/10 pain across two consecutive weeks at current ROM.
- Stable knee in frontal plane during single-leg tasks (no valgus).
- Able to complete reverse sled drags heavy without pain flare.
- If all met, lower box/seat by 1–2 cm the following week, within phase ROM caps.

Notes for return-to-snow readiness
- Emphasize even weight shifts in wall-sit holds and slideboard. Cue tripod foot, knee tracking over 2nd–3rd toe, quiet upper body with strong anti-rotation.
- Keep building adductors (Copenhagen) and lateral drags—they’re key for edging and carving control.
- No jumping or deep loaded flexion throughout the 12 weeks unless explicitly cleared and symptom-free.

This structure gives you clear weekly progressions while protecting the meniscus, building total-body strength, and layering in ski-specific lateral control and endurance. Adjust weekly based on the knee’s response and the surgeon/PT’s guidance.
